fields.name: Failed Logins
fields.description: Detect failed login attempts which may indicate brute-force or unauthorized access attempts.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may be attempting to gain access through password guessing or brute-force attacks.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4625 | stats count by user, src_ip, host | sort -count
fields.expected_evidence: Multiple failed login events (4625) from same source IP or targeting same user account.
fields.investigation_notes: Check if failed logins are followed by a successful login (4624). Review the source IP reputation. Verify if the account exists.

fields.name: Successful Logins
fields.description: Review successful login events to identify unusual access patterns.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use valid credentials to access systems at unusual times or from unusual locations.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4624 | stats count by user, src_ip, LogonType, host | sort -count
fields.expected_evidence: Login events (4624) from unexpected IPs, at unusual hours, or with unusual logon types.
fields.investigation_notes: Compare against known user behavior patterns. Check LogonType: 2=Interactive, 3=Network, 10=RemoteInteractive(RDP).

fields.name: Brute Force Detection
fields.description: Detect multiple failed logins followed by a successful login, indicating potential brute-force success.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may have successfully brute-forced a user account password.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4625 OR EventCode=4624) | stats count(eval(EventCode=4625)) as failures, count(eval(EventCode=4624)) as successes by user, src_ip | where failures > 5 AND successes > 0 | sort -failures
fields.expected_evidence: High number of failed logins followed by a successful login from the same source.
fields.investigation_notes: This is a strong indicator of brute-force. Check the timing between failures and success. Review what the account did after successful login.

fields.name: New Account Creation
fields.description: Detect creation of new local user accounts.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may create a new local account for persistence.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4720 | table _time, host, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, SubjectDomainName | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: Event 4720 showing a new account being created, especially by non-standard accounts.
fields.investigation_notes: Check who created the account (SubjectUserName). Verify if this was an authorized change. Look for subsequent privileged group additions (4732, 4728).

fields.name: Privileged Group Membership Changes
fields.description: Detect when users are added to privileged groups (Administrators, Domain Admins, etc.).
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may escalate privileges by adding a compromised or newly created account to an administrator group.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4728 OR EventCode=4732 OR EventCode=4756) | table _time, host, SubjectUserName, MemberName, TargetUserName, GroupName | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: Events showing users being added to privileged security groups.
fields.investigation_notes: Cross-reference with account creation events. Verify if the group change was authorized. Check what the newly privileged account did afterward.

fields.name: PowerShell Execution
fields.description: Detect PowerShell process execution, especially with suspicious parameters.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use PowerShell for command execution, script downloads, or lateral movement.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) (NewProcessName="*powershell*" OR Image="*powershell*" OR ParentImage="*powershell*") | table _time, host, user, CommandLine, ParentImage, Image, NewProcessName | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: PowerShell processes, especially those with encoded commands (-enc), download cradles, or running from unusual parents.
fields.investigation_notes: Decode any base64 encoded commands. Check the parent process — is it unusual (e.g., winword.exe spawning powershell)? Review network connections made by PowerShell.

fields.name: Encoded PowerShell Commands
fields.description: Detect PowerShell with encoded or obfuscated command-line arguments.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may encode PowerShell commands to evade detection.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) (CommandLine="*-enc*" OR CommandLine="*-encodedcommand*" OR CommandLine="*-e *" OR CommandLine="*FromBase64*" OR CommandLine="*[Convert]*") | table _time, host, user, CommandLine, ParentImage | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: PowerShell processes with -enc, -encodedcommand, or Base64 decoding in the command line.
fields.investigation_notes: Decode the Base64 payload to understand what it actually does. This is a strong indicator of malicious activity but can also be used by legitimate admin scripts.

fields.name: Suspicious Command Shell Execution
fields.description: Detect cmd.exe execution with suspicious parent processes or command patterns.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use cmd.exe for command execution or to chain commands.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) (NewProcessName="*cmd.exe*" OR Image="*cmd.exe*") | table _time, host, user, CommandLine, ParentImage, Image | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: cmd.exe launched by unusual parent processes or with suspicious command patterns.
fields.investigation_notes: Review the parent process — was cmd.exe spawned by a document editor, browser, or service? Check if the command line reveals reconnaissance or malicious activity.

fields.name: New Service Installation
fields.description: Detect installation of new Windows services which may be used for persistence.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may install a malicious service for persistence.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=7045 | table _time, host, ServiceName, ImagePath, ServiceType, StartType, AccountName | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: New service installations (7045), especially with unusual service names, image paths, or running as SYSTEM.
fields.investigation_notes: Verify if the service is legitimate. Check the ImagePath for suspicious executables. Review if the service was installed during off-hours.

fields.name: Process Creation Analysis
fields.description: Analyze process creation events to identify suspicious parent-child relationships.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may create processes with unusual parent-child relationships indicating exploitation.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) | table _time, host, user, NewProcessName, Image, ParentImage, CommandLine, ProcessId, ParentProcessId | sort -_time | head 200
fields.expected_evidence: Unusual process trees (e.g., winword.exe → powershell.exe → cmd.exe).
fields.investigation_notes: Focus on processes spawned by document editors, browsers, or services. Look for LOLBins (Living Off The Land Binaries) like rundll32, mshta, regsvr32.

fields.name: RDP Activity
fields.description: Detect Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) logins and activity.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use RDP for lateral movement after obtaining valid credentials.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4624 LogonType=10 | stats count by user, src_ip, host | sort -count
fields.expected_evidence: RDP logins (LogonType=10) from unusual source IPs or to sensitive systems.
fields.investigation_notes: Verify if the RDP session was authorized. Check what the user did during the session. Review if there are multiple RDP sessions from the same source.

fields.name: SMB/Network Logons
fields.description: Detect network logons via SMB which may indicate lateral movement.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use SMB for lateral movement or to access network shares.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4624 LogonType=3 | stats count by user, src_ip, host | sort -count
fields.expected_evidence: Network logons (LogonType=3) from unusual sources or in unusual patterns.
fields.investigation_notes: Not all LogonType=3 is malicious — file shares generate these too. Focus on unusual source IPs and access to sensitive systems.

fields.name: Archive/Compression Utility Usage
fields.description: Detect use of archive utilities that may indicate data staging or exfiltration preparation.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may compress collected data before exfiltration.
fields.spl: index=threathunt (EventCode=4688 OR EventCode=1) (CommandLine="*7z*" OR CommandLine="*rar*" OR CommandLine="*zip*" OR CommandLine="*tar*" OR Image="*7z*" OR Image="*WinRAR*") | table _time, host, user, CommandLine, Image, ParentImage | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: Execution of archiving utilities, especially targeting sensitive directories.
fields.investigation_notes: Check what files/folders are being archived. Review if the archive is then moved to an external location. Verify if the archiving was part of normal operations.

fields.name: LSASS Access Detection
fields.description: Detect processes accessing LSASS memory, which may indicate credential dumping.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may attempt to dump credentials from LSASS process memory.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=10 TargetImage="*lsass.exe" | table _time, host, user, SourceImage, TargetImage, GrantedAccess, CallTrace | sort -_time
fields.expected_evidence: Sysmon Event ID 10 showing process access to lsass.exe, especially from unusual source processes.
fields.investigation_notes: Some legitimate processes access LSASS (e.g., antivirus). Focus on unusual SourceImage values and GrantedAccess flags (0x1010, 0x1FFFFF are suspicious). Distinguish observed evidence from confirmed credential theft.

fields.name: Privileged Account Usage
fields.description: Detect usage of special privileges assigned to new logon sessions.
fields.hypothesis: An attacker may use privileged accounts for malicious activity after gaining access.
fields.spl: index=threathunt EventCode=4672 | stats count by user, host | sort -count
fields.expected_evidence: Privileged logons (4672) by unusual accounts or at unusual times.
fields.investigation_notes: EventCode 4672 fires when special privileges are assigned. Common for SYSTEM and administrator accounts. Focus on non-service accounts receiving privileges.
